text:
Mateo Alvarez: Kicking off the Hardware tuning profiles pack work (kernel + scheduling). Goal is a *versioned* profile pack per SKU (H100/B200/L40S) w/ expected behavior docs + rollout safety. We’re targeting runtime-1.22 train.

Mateo Alvarez: Epic is up here: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4921 (please subscribe)

Mateo Alvarez: I dropped an initial Confluence outline (very rough) under Eng > Serving Runtime > Kernel + Scheduling. We’ll flesh out as we go.

Talia Benson: +1. Can we lock owners today so we can start moving tasks from “Draft” -> “In progress”? Also need a single place for links (docs/PRs/bench runs).

Noah Patel: Agree. Suggest we treat this like a mini “release feature”: schema + selection + observability + perf gating + docs. Owners per track + weekly checkpoint.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel side: I can own the H100 attention variant selection + fallback rules. Likely needs Grace + Yuki for implementation + stability counters.

Grace Kim: Yep, I can take the implementation slice (kernel choice plumbing + metrics). Will need clarity on how profile IDs map to kernel variants.

Yuki Sato: I can own “kernel auto-selection + safety”: compatibility gates (driver/CUDA) and “refuse unsafe defaults” behavior esp for early B200.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduling: I’ll own workload buckets + queue policy defaults. I want Marcus/Lena in the loop since they’ve been closest to mixed prompt length issues.

Marcus Reed: I can take queue management + perf suite tie-in (at least from runtime side). Biggest risk is p99 under mixed workloads.

Lena Fischer: I can implement backpressure / concurrency caps per profile once we agree on the knobs + guardrails.

Rina Kobayashi: Benchmark harness: I own benchmark-lab side. I can draft the benchmark matrix + acceptance thresholds, but I’ll need Applied ML to sanity-check workload buckets + model set.

Claire Dubois: I’ll help on methodology (prompt/response distributions + noise handling). Also want to ensure “expected behavior” docs aren’t just benchmark numbers but actual tradeoffs / failure modes.

Arjun Desai: I’ll review quantization interactions (esp any profile knobs that change memory headroom / KV behavior). Also want a slot for “quality regression risk” notes where relevant.

Elliot Price: Docs: I can own the Confluence set (overview + schema + expected behavior per SKU + rollout/runbook). Kira can help with runbook structure + troubleshooting.

Kira Thompson: Yep. If we can get a list of “signals to check” from SRE/Obs (queueing, kernel fallbacks, fragmentation, OOM) I’ll incorporate into the troubleshooting sections.

Allison Grant: Observability: I can own metric naming + dashboard spec. Please keep tag cardinality in mind (profile_id/sku ok; per-model is trickier). We should standardize the tags now so perf-canary/benchmark-lab can consume.

Sean Gallagher: SRE ask: we need explicit rollout SLO gates + a kill switch semantics doc. Don’t want to be arguing during a tail-lat incident.

Rafael Mendes: +1. I can draft canary cohorts + rollback steps. We should decide what we roll back (profile version vs individual knobs) and how quickly.

Neha Kapoor: Infra constraints: Irene and I can provide the SKU/instance type mapping + driver/CUDA baselines (and where we have variance). Compatibility checks need to match reality.

Irene Choi: I’ll post current fleet constraints (H100 PCIe vs SXM, MIG policy, CUDA baseline). For B200 we’ll have early heterogeneity; we should assume “gate hard” until baseline settles.

Connor O'Brien: Release Eng: I need (1) a versioning plan for the profile pack, (2) what qualifies as a patch vs minor bump, (3) what needs to be in runtime-1.22 vs can be follow-up. Also please keep a changelog for profile changes.

Sahana Iyer: CI/perf gating: I can own “block merges on invalid profile defs” + perf-canary gating rules (warn vs fail). But I need the benchmark matrix + acceptance thresholds early.

Talia Benson: Summarizing owners (please confirm):
- Kernel tuning (H100 + fallback rules): Hiro (Grace/Yuki)
- Scheduler tuning (workload buckets/queue policy): Sofia (Marcus/Lena)
- Benchmark matrix + acceptance thresholds: Rina (Claire/Arjun)
- Observability + dashboards: Allison (w/ input from Omar once KV signals land)
- Rollout SLO gates / runbook / kill switch: Sean + Rafael
- Infra constraints + compatibility inputs: Neha + Irene
- Docs (Confluence set): Elliot + Kira
- Release process / versioning discipline: Connor
- CI/perf gating wiring: Sahana

Omar El-Sayed: For KV/memory observability: I can add counters for compaction time + fragmentation estimates once we align on what’s “expected” vs “alertable.” I’ll coordinate w/ Allison on metric names.

Mateo Alvarez: Looks right to me. If anyone disagrees, speak now.

Linear Bot: ENG-4921 updated: added labels [runtime] [perf] [release-1.22] and assigned Program Manager: Talia Benson

Mateo Alvarez: Next steps (this week):
1) Talia schedule 30min kickoff sync (goal: agree on schema + selection boundaries + the initial benchmark matrix).
2) Elliot create Confluence pages placeholders so we can link from PRs (even if empty for now).
3) Rina/Claire draft benchmark matrix v1 + “what is pass/fail” for H100 + L40S.
4) Allison propose metric/tag set (profile_id, profile_version, sku, scheduling_mode) and 1 dashboard mock.
5) Neha/Irene post fleet baselines + known heterogeneity (driver/CUDA/MIG).

Mateo Alvarez: Links to draft docs (WIP):
- Overview doc (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/serving-runtime/profiles-pack/overview
- Schema + selection rules (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/serving-runtime/profiles-pack/schema-selection

Hiro Tanaka: Confirmed. I’ll start with a quick kernel variant comparison summary for H100 (what we think “v3” vs “v2” does + when to fallback). Will drop notes in the overview doc.

Sofia Ivanova: Confirmed. I’ll draft initial workload buckets (short/med/long prefill + decode heavy) and a proposal for queue limits/backpressure knobs.

Rina Kobayashi: Confirmed. I’ll create a sheet for matrix v1 and link it from ENG-4921. Need to decide model set (at least 2 chat LLMs + 1 long-context) + embeddings?

Claire Dubois: For v1 I’d keep embeddings out unless we explicitly want it in scope; otherwise matrix explodes. But we should at least call it out as non-goal / future.

Mateo Alvarez: Agree, keep embeddings out of the initial perf gate. Focus on text/chat decode/prefill patterns.

Allison Grant: I’ll post a draft metrics map today. Please don’t add new metric names in PRs without checking in; we’ll end up with 6 variants of the same thing :)

Sean Gallagher: If we can get a decision on kill switch: “disable profile pack” should revert to pre-1.22 defaults *without redeploy* (config flip). That’s the bar.

Noah Patel: +1. Also selection logic: I prefer deterministic at runtime startup w/ explicit logging (active profile + detected hardware + any overrides). Makes on-call easier.

Connor O'Brien: Please also tag the profile pack version in /health and/or debug endpoint. Helpful for go/no-go and customer escalations.

Mateo Alvarez: Great. Let’s do it. :thumbsup:

Talia Benson: I’ll send calendar + a short agenda. Please add any open questions to ENG-4921 before the sync.

Marcus Reed: One ask: can we explicitly track “p99 regression risk” in the acceptance thresholds? Not just “mean tps improved.”

Sahana Iyer: Yep, can do. If we have defined thresholds per SKU/workload, perf-canary can block on p95/p99 deltas.

Yuki Sato: Last thing: for B200 early fleet, I want a hard gate: require explicit profile_version pin until we bless defaults. Otherwise we’ll chase driver/CUDA mismatches.

Neha Kapoor: Works for Infra. We’ll share the baseline plan; there will be exceptions at first.

Mateo Alvarez: Sounds like consensus. Thread can stay open for links/updates.
